analyses.title: Dropbox supports batch multi-select in manual upload picker; Google Photos manual backup is per-item via touch-and-hold
analyses.description:
In the manual upload entry points documented on official help pages, Dropbox mobile instructs users to 'Tap the photos you would like to upload' after choosing Upload Photos, implying multi-select on Android; Google Photos Android manual backup requires opening a single photo and tapping 'Back up now,' with a tip noting that to back up multiple items users should 'Touch and hold the photos or videos you want to back up, and then tap Back up.' Subject to human review.
【推断】场景：Manual photo upload entry points on Google Photos Android vs Dropbox mobile (official help pages)

analyses.title: Scenario-relative strengths and weaknesses of each app's manual upload entry point
analyses.description:
In the manual upload scenario, Google Photos Android's strength is unified backup semantics (single 'Back up now' action tied to the existing backup pipeline, with status cues such as 'Not enough storage to back up'); its weakness is the open-one-item-then-back-up flow, which, per official help, requires touch-and-hold to back up multiple items. Dropbox mobile's strength is a deliberate multi-step flow with explicit folder/destination selection ('Tap the folder icon (Android) or Next (iOS)') and a Set location step; its weakness, per official help, is the Windows-app restriction ('The Dropbox app for Windows devices does not currently support video uploads') and reliance on being logged in to Dropbox. Subject to human review.
【推断】场景：Manual photo upload entry points on Google Photos Android vs Dropbox mobile (official help pages)

analyses.title: Both apps pair an automatic backup feature with a manual entry point on Android
analyses.description:
Across the two sampled products, both Google Photos Android and Dropbox mobile document a manual upload/backup entry point that coexists with an automatic backup feature: Google Photos' automatic backup is set up via 'turn on backup,' while Dropbox documents 'Camera uploads' as the automatic counterpart and a '+ → Upload Photos' flow as the manual counterpart. This pattern of pairing automatic + manual upload entry points is observed in both samples. Subject to human review.
【推断】场景：Manual photo upload entry points on Google Photos Android vs Dropbox mobile (official help pages)

analyses.title: Risk of documentation ambiguity when users expect multi-select but the default flow is single-item
analyses.description:
Per Google Photos official help, the default manual backup flow is to open a single photo and tap 'Back up now,' with multi-item back up described only as a tip ('Touch and hold the photos or videos you want to back up'). Inferred risk: users expecting multi-select as the default may not discover this tip, leading to repeated single-item taps. Dropbox documents 'Tap the photos you would like to upload' as part of the main procedure, suggesting multi-select is the main path. Subject to human review.
【推断】场景：Manual photo upload entry points on Google Photos Android vs Dropbox mobile (official help pages)

analyses.title: Recommendation: clarify Google Photos multi-item back-up path in the main manual-backup steps
analyses.description:
Recommendation for human review: promote the multi-item back-up tip ('Touch and hold the photos or videos you want to back up, and then tap Back up') from a tips subsection into the numbered manual-back-up procedure, so users do not need to discover batch selection via secondary text. This is a documentation-level proposal only and does not modify product decisions or claim behavioral outcomes.
【建议】场景：Manual photo upload entry points on Google Photos Android vs Dropbox mobile (official help pages)
